blocks.en: The Lamb of God: Trial, Cross, and Tomb
blocks.es_reference: El Cordero de Dios: juicio, cruz y sepulcro

blocks.en: The Trials, the Crucifixion, the Seven Words, the Death, and the Burial
blocks.es_reference: Los juicios, la crucifixión, las siete palabras, la muerte y la sepultura

blocks.en: 1. The Trials
blocks.es_reference: 1. Los juicios

blocks.en: They led Him first to the high priests, Annas and then Caiaphas, and the council sought testimony to put Him to death but found only false and conflicting witnesses. At last the high priest demanded, "Are You the Christ, the Son of the Blessed?" And Jesus answered plainly, "I am. And you will see the Son of Man... coming with the clouds of heaven" (Mark 14:61–62). The high priest tore his clothes and cried, "He has spoken blasphemy!" They judged Him worthy of death, then spat on Him, struck Him, and mocked Him.
blocks.es_reference: Lo llevaron primero ante los sumos sacerdotes, Anás y luego Caifás, y el concilio buscaba testimonio para darle muerte, mas solo halló testigos falsos y discordantes. Al fin el sumo sacerdote le exigió: “¿Eres tú el Cristo, el Hijo del Bendito?” Y Jesús respondió claramente: “Yo soy; y veréis al Hijo del Hombre... viniendo en las nubes del cielo” (Marcos 14:61–62). El sumo sacerdote rasgó sus vestiduras y clamó: “¡Ha blasfemado!” Le juzgaron reo de muerte, y luego le escupieron, le golpearon y se burlaron de Él.

blocks.en: Outside in the courtyard the brave promise of the night before collapsed. Three times Peter was asked if he knew the Man, and three times he denied it, the last with oaths. Then the rooster crowed, and the Lord turned and looked at Peter; and Peter remembered the word, went out, and "wept bitterly" (Luke 22:61–62).
blocks.es_reference: Afuera, en el patio, la valiente promesa de la noche anterior se derrumbó. Tres veces preguntaron a Pedro si conocía al Hombre, y tres veces lo negó, la última con juramentos. Entonces cantó el gallo, y el Señor se volvió y miró a Pedro; y Pedro recordó la palabra, salió fuera y “lloró amargamente” (Lucas 22:61–62).

blocks.en: At dawn they handed Him to Pilate. "Are You the King of the Jews?" Pilate examined Him and declared, "I find no fault in this Man" (Luke 23:4). Even Pilate's wife sent word to him, "Have nothing to do with that just Man, for I have suffered many things... in a dream because of Him" (Matthew 27:19); and when Jesus spoke of bearing witness to the truth, Pilate only shrugged, "What is truth?" (John 18:38) — truth itself standing bound before him. He sent Him to Herod, who mocked Him and sent Him back. Seeking to release Him, Pilate offered the crowd a choice between Jesus and a murderer named Barabbas; but the chief priests stirred the people, who cried, "Barabbas!" and "Crucify Him!" Pilate washed his hands before them, "I am innocent of the blood of this just Person," and the people answered, "His blood be on us and on our children" (Matthew 27:24–25). Then he had Jesus scourged. The soldiers twisted a crown of thorns for His head, threw a purple robe on Him, and mocked, "Hail, King of the Jews!" striking Him; and Pilate brought Him out, "Behold the Man!" (John 19:5). When Pilate boasted of his authority, Jesus answered, "You could have no power at all against Me unless it had been given you from above" (John 19:11); and at last Pilate yielded Him up to be crucified.
blocks.es_reference: Al amanecer le entregaron a Pilato. “¿Eres tú el Rey de los judíos?” Pilato le examinó y declaró: “Ninguna falta hallo en este hombre” (Lucas 23:4). Aun la mujer de Pilato le mandó decir: “No tengas nada que ver con ese justo; porque hoy he padecido mucho en sueños por causa de Él” (Mateo 27:19); y cuando Jesús habló de dar testimonio de la verdad, Pilato solo se encogió: “¿Qué es la verdad?” (Juan 18:38) — la verdad misma de pie, atada, ante él. Le envió a Herodes, que se burló de Él y se lo devolvió. Buscando soltarle, Pilato ofreció a la multitud escoger entre Jesús y un homicida llamado Barrabás; pero los principales sacerdotes incitaron al pueblo, que clamó: “¡Barrabás!” y “¡Crucifícale!” Pilato se lavó las manos delante de ellos: “Inocente soy yo de la sangre de este justo,” y el pueblo respondió: “Su sangre sea sobre nosotros, y sobre nuestros hijos” (Mateo 27:24–25). Entonces mandó azotar a Jesús. Los soldados trenzaron una corona de espinas para su cabeza, le echaron un manto de púrpura y se burlaron: “¡Salve, Rey de los judíos!” golpeándole; y Pilato le sacó: “¡He aquí el hombre!” (Juan 19:5). Cuando Pilato se jactó de su autoridad, Jesús respondió: “Ninguna potestad tendrías contra mí, si no te fuese dado de arriba” (Juan 19:11); y al fin Pilato le entregó para ser crucificado.

blocks.en: 2. The Crucifixion
blocks.es_reference: 2. La crucifixión

blocks.en: They led Him out to Golgotha, the place of a skull. Worn from the scourging, He could no longer carry the cross, so the soldiers compelled Simon of Cyrene to bear it behind Him. A crowd of women followed, weeping, and He turned to them: "Daughters of Jerusalem, do not weep for Me, but weep for yourselves and for your children" (Luke 23:28), for He saw the judgment coming on the city.
blocks.es_reference: Le sacaron al Gólgota, el lugar de la calavera. Agotado por los azotes, ya no podía cargar la cruz, así que los soldados obligaron a Simón de Cirene a llevarla tras Él. Una multitud de mujeres le seguía, llorando, y Él se volvió a ellas: “Hijas de Jerusalén, no lloréis por mí, sino llorad por vosotras mismas y por vuestros hijos” (Lucas 23:28), porque veía el juicio que venía sobre la ciudad.

blocks.en: There they crucified Him, and with Him two robbers, one on the right and one on the left. Over His head they fixed the written charge, "THIS IS JESUS THE KING OF THE JEWS." And the soldiers took His garments and cast lots for His robe, fulfilling the ancient word, "They divide My garments among them, and for My clothing they cast lots" (Psalm 22:18).
blocks.es_reference: Allí le crucificaron, y con Él a dos ladrones, uno a la derecha y otro a la izquierda. Sobre su cabeza fijaron la acusación escrita: “ESTE ES JESÚS EL REY DE LOS JUDÍOS.” Y los soldados tomaron sus vestidos y echaron suertes sobre su túnica, cumpliendo la antigua palabra: “Repartieron entre sí mis vestidos, y sobre mi ropa echaron suertes” (Salmo 22:18).

blocks.en: Those who passed by mocked Him, wagging their heads: "He saved others; Himself He cannot save. If He is the King of Israel, let Him now come down from the cross, and we will believe Him" (Matthew 27:42). Even the two robbers reviled Him at first; but one of them, hanging there in his own agony, came to his senses and turned to the dying King beside him.
blocks.es_reference: Los que pasaban se burlaban de Él, meneando la cabeza: “A otros salvó, a sí mismo no se puede salvar. Si es el Rey de Israel, descienda ahora de la cruz, y creeremos en Él” (Mateo 27:42). Aun los dos ladrones le injuriaban al principio; pero uno de ellos, colgado allí en su propia agonía, volvió en sí y se volvió al Rey moribundo a su lado.

blocks.en: 3. The Seven Words from the Cross
blocks.es_reference: 3. Las siete palabras desde la cruz

blocks.en: From the cross He spoke seven times, and each word is a window into His heart.
blocks.es_reference: Desde la cruz habló siete veces, y cada palabra es una ventana a su corazón.

blocks.en: First, for His executioners: "Father, forgive them, for they do not know what they do" (Luke 23:34). Second, to the dying thief who rebuked the other — "we receive the due reward of our deeds, but this Man has done nothing wrong" — and then turned to Christ, "Lord, remember me when You come into Your kingdom," He promised, "Assuredly, I say to you, today you will be with Me in Paradise" (Luke 23:43) — that very day, in conscious joy, with Christ. Third, seeing His mother and the disciple John, He gave her into John's care: "Woman, behold your son!... Behold your mother!" (John 19:26–27).
blocks.es_reference: Primera, por sus verdugos: “Padre, perdónalos, porque no saben lo que hacen” (Lucas 23:34). Segunda, al ladrón moribundo que reprendió al otro — “nosotros recibimos lo que merecieron nuestros hechos; mas este ningún mal hizo” — y luego se volvió a Cristo: “Señor, acuérdate de mí cuando vengas en tu reino,” le prometió: “De cierto te digo que hoy estarás conmigo en el paraíso” (Lucas 23:43) — ese mismo día, en gozo consciente, con Cristo. Tercera, viendo a su madre y al discípulo Juan, la encomendó al cuidado de Juan: “Mujer, he ahí tu hijo... He ahí tu madre” (Juan 19:26–27).

blocks.en: Then, from noon, darkness covered the land, and out of it came the fourth word, the cry of dereliction: "My God, My God, why have You forsaken Me?" (Matthew 27:46), the opening of Psalm 22. In that hour He bore the judgment our sin deserved, drinking to the dregs the forsaking that was ours, that we might never be forsaken. It was not that the Father had ceased to love the Son; it was that the Son, bearing our sin, tasted in our place the abandonment that sin deserves. Fifth, "I thirst" (John 19:28) — true human anguish, and Scripture fulfilled. Sixth came the cry of triumph: "It is finished" (John 19:30) — a single word in the Greek, tetelestai. And seventh, in willing surrender: "Father, into Your hands I commit My spirit" (Luke 23:46); and having said this, He gave up His spirit. No man took His life; He laid it down. Even in His dying He was Lord of His own death.
blocks.es_reference: Entonces, desde el mediodía, las tinieblas cubrieron la tierra, y de ellas vino la cuarta palabra, el clamor de abandono: “Dios mío, Dios mío, ¿por qué me has desamparado?” (Mateo 27:46), el comienzo del Salmo 22. En aquella hora llevó el juicio que nuestro pecado merecía, bebiendo hasta las heces el desamparo que era nuestro, para que nosotros nunca fuésemos desamparados. No fue que el Padre dejara de amar al Hijo; fue que el Hijo, llevando nuestro pecado, gustó en nuestro lugar el abandono que el pecado merece. Quinta: “Tengo sed” (Juan 19:28) — verdadera angustia humana, y la Escritura cumplida. Sexta vino el clamor de triunfo: “Consumado es” (Juan 19:30) — una sola palabra en el griego, tetelestai. Y séptima, en entrega voluntaria: “Padre, en tus manos encomiendo mi espíritu” (Lucas 23:46); y habiendo dicho esto, entregó el espíritu. Ningún hombre le quitó la vida; Él la puso. Aun en su morir era Señor de su propia muerte.

blocks.en: In the old markets a paid debt was stamped with one word — tetelestai, "paid in full." That is the word Jesus cried from the cross. The debt of our sin was not reduced, nor rescheduled, nor partly covered; it was paid, in full, forever.
blocks.es_reference: En los antiguos mercados, una deuda pagada se sellaba con una sola palabra — tetelestai, “pagado por completo.” Esa es la palabra que Jesús clamó desde la cruz. La deuda de nuestro pecado no fue reducida, ni reprogramada, ni cubierta a medias; fue pagada, por completo, para siempre.

blocks.en: 4. The Death and Its Signs
blocks.es_reference: 4. La muerte y sus señales

blocks.en: The death of the Son of God shook heaven and earth. The veil of the temple, the heavy curtain that barred the way into the Most Holy Place, was torn in two "from top to bottom" (Matthew 27:51) — torn from heaven downward, by no human hand, for the way into God's presence was now opened through His blood. Behind that veil had stood the Most Holy Place, where only the high priest could enter, and only once a year, and never without blood. Now it hung open from top to bottom: the death of the Lamb had opened a new and living way for every believer to draw near to God. The earth quaked and the rocks split. And the Roman centurion who stood watch, seeing how He died, confessed, "Truly this was the Son of God!" (Matthew 27:54) — a pagan soldier saying what the council had denied.
blocks.es_reference: La muerte del Hijo de Dios sacudió cielo y tierra. El velo del templo, la pesada cortina que cerraba el paso al Lugar Santísimo, se rasgó en dos “de arriba abajo” (Mateo 27:51) — rasgado desde el cielo hacia abajo, por ninguna mano humana, porque ya se había abierto el camino a la presencia de Dios por su sangre. Tras aquel velo había estado el Lugar Santísimo, donde solo el sumo sacerdote podía entrar, y solo una vez al año, y nunca sin sangre. Ahora colgaba abierto de arriba abajo: la muerte del Cordero había abierto un camino nuevo y vivo para que todo creyente se acerque a Dios. La tierra tembló y las rocas se partieron. Y el centurión romano que montaba guardia, viendo cómo murió, confesó: “Verdaderamente este era el Hijo de Dios” (Mateo 27:54) — un soldado pagano diciendo lo que el concilio había negado.

blocks.en: And there is a further wonder hidden in that torn curtain. By the time of Herod's temple the Most Holy Place stood empty — the ark of the covenant, with its mercy seat, had vanished centuries before, lost when Babylon destroyed the first temple, and the glory of God had long since departed (Ezekiel 10–11). For nearly six hundred years the high priest had entered once a year into a bare room that held only a stone. So when the veil was torn from top to bottom, it opened upon an empty chamber — because the meeting place between God and man was no longer there. It had moved to the cross. Paul calls the crucified Christ our "propitiation" (Romans 3:25) — the very word the Greek Old Testament used for the mercy seat. The true Mercy Seat was no longer hidden behind a curtain in an empty room; it was lifted up on a hill, sprinkled not with the blood of bulls and goats but with the blood of the Son. God tore the veil to say: stop searching the empty room — here, in My Son, is where heaven and earth now meet.
blocks.es_reference: Y hay una maravilla más escondida en aquella cortina rasgada. Para los días del templo de Herodes, el Lugar Santísimo estaba vacío — el arca del pacto, con su propiciatorio, había desaparecido siglos atrás, perdida cuando Babilonia destruyó el primer templo, y la gloria de Dios hacía mucho que se había apartado (Ezequiel 10–11). Por casi seiscientos años el sumo sacerdote había entrado una vez al año en una sala desnuda que solo guardaba una piedra. Así que cuando el velo se rasgó de arriba abajo, se abrió sobre una cámara vacía — porque el lugar de encuentro entre Dios y el hombre ya no estaba allí. Se había trasladado a la cruz. Pablo llama al Cristo crucificado nuestra “propiciación” (Romanos 3:25) — la misma palabra que el Antiguo Testamento griego usó para el propiciatorio. El verdadero Propiciatorio ya no estaba oculto tras una cortina en una sala vacía; estaba levantado en un monte, rociado no con la sangre de toros y machos cabríos, sino con la sangre del Hijo. Dios rasgó el velo para decir: dejen de buscar en la sala vacía — aquí, en mi Hijo, es donde ahora se encuentran el cielo y la tierra.

blocks.en: To make certain He was dead, a soldier pierced His side with a spear, and "immediately blood and water came out" (John 19:34): He was truly, fully dead. Yet they did not break His legs as they broke the others', and so another Scripture was fulfilled: "Not one of His bones shall be broken" (John 19:36) — for He is the true Passover Lamb, whose bones were never to be broken.
blocks.es_reference: Para cerciorarse de que estaba muerto, un soldado le traspasó el costado con una lanza, y “al instante salió sangre y agua” (Juan 19:34): estaba verdadera y plenamente muerto. Mas no le quebraron las piernas como a los otros, y así se cumplió otra Escritura: “No será quebrado hueso suyo” (Juan 19:36) — porque Él es el verdadero Cordero pascual, cuyos huesos nunca habían de ser quebrados.

blocks.en: 5. The Burial and the Meaning of the Cross
blocks.es_reference: 5. La sepultura y el sentido de la cruz

blocks.en: Then Joseph of Arimathea, a disciple who had followed in secret, took courage and asked Pilate for the body. With Nicodemus, who brought about a hundred pounds of myrrh and aloes, he wrapped it in linen with the spices and laid it in his own new tomb, cut from the rock, where no one had yet lain, and rolled a great stone across the door (John 19:38–42). So He was "with the rich in His death," as the prophet had foretold (Isaiah 53:9). The women watched where He was laid. And the chief priests, still afraid, set a guard and sealed the stone (Matthew 27:62–66).
blocks.es_reference: Entonces José de Arimatea, un discípulo que había seguido en secreto, cobró ánimo y pidió a Pilato el cuerpo. Con Nicodemo, que trajo como cien libras de mirra y áloes, lo envolvió en lienzos con las especias y lo puso en su propio sepulcro nuevo, abierto en la roca, donde nadie aún había sido puesto, y rodó una gran piedra a la entrada (Juan 19:38–42). Así fue “con los ricos en su muerte,” como el profeta había anunciado (Isaías 53:9). Las mujeres miraban dónde le ponían. Y los principales sacerdotes, aún temerosos, pusieron guardia y sellaron la piedra (Mateo 27:62–66).

blocks.en: What, then, does the cross mean? The Lamb of God was slain in our place. "It is finished" declares the price of sin paid in full; the torn veil declares the way to God thrown open; the forsaken cry tells us He bore the judgment we deserved, so that all who trust Him will never be forsaken. This is the heart of the gospel: He died for our sins, the just for the unjust, to bring us to God. Barabbas had felt it first in his own flesh: the guilty man walked free because Another took the cross that was his. So it is for every sinner who trusts Him — the innocent died, and the guilty go free. This is grace: His death counted as ours, and His righteousness given to us in exchange.
blocks.es_reference: ¿Qué significa, pues, la cruz? El Cordero de Dios fue inmolado en nuestro lugar. “Consumado es” declara el precio del pecado pagado por completo; el velo rasgado declara el camino a Dios abierto de par en par; el clamor de abandono nos dice que llevó el juicio que merecíamos, para que todo el que confía en Él nunca sea desamparado. Este es el corazón del evangelio: murió por nuestros pecados, el justo por los injustos, para llevarnos a Dios. Barrabás lo sintió primero en su propia carne: el culpable quedó libre porque Otro tomó la cruz que era suya. Así es para todo pecador que confía en Él — el inocente murió, y los culpables quedan libres. Esto es la gracia: su muerte contada como nuestra, y su justicia dada a nosotros a cambio.

blocks.en: And the divine and human stand together to the last. The eternal Son died as a man, commending His spirit to the Father; the Lord of glory was wrapped in linen and laid in a borrowed grave. The death was real, the price was paid, and the Lamb was slain. The stone was rolled, the seal was set, the guard was posted — and all of it, in three days, would be undone. For the grave that received the Lamb of God could not be its keeper.
blocks.es_reference: Y lo divino y lo humano están juntos hasta el fin. El Hijo eterno murió como hombre, encomendando su espíritu al Padre; el Señor de gloria fue envuelto en lienzos y puesto en una tumba prestada. La muerte fue real, el precio fue pagado, y el Cordero fue inmolado. La piedra fue rodada, el sello fue puesto, la guardia fue apostada — y todo ello, en tres días, sería deshecho. Porque la tumba que recibió al Cordero de Dios no podía ser su guardiana.

sa.prompt: Describe the Jewish trial and Peter's denial (Mark 14; Luke 22).
sa.model: Led before Annas and Caiaphas, Jesus faced false witnesses. When the high priest asked if He was the Christ, the Son of the Blessed, He answered “I am,” and the priest tore his clothes, crying blasphemy; they judged Him worthy of death. Meanwhile Peter denied Him three times in the courtyard, and when the rooster crowed and the Lord looked at him, he went out and wept bitterly.

sa.prompt: Describe the Roman trial before Pilate (Matt 27; Luke 23; John 18-19).
sa.model: Pilate examined Jesus and declared, “I find no fault in this Man,” even after his wife warned him. He offered the crowd a choice, but they cried for Barabbas the murderer and “Crucify Him.” Pilate washed his hands, and the people said, “His blood be on us.” He had Jesus scourged; the soldiers crowned Him with thorns, robed Him in purple, and mocked, “Hail, King of the Jews.”

sa.prompt: Describe the crucifixion at Golgotha (Luke 23; Matt 27; Psalm 22).
sa.model: Too weak to carry the cross, Jesus had Simon of Cyrene compelled to bear it to Golgotha. He told the weeping women to weep for themselves. There they crucified Him between two robbers, fixed the charge “King of the Jews” above His head, and cast lots for His garments, fulfilling Psalm 22. The passersby and one of the robbers mocked Him at first.

sa.prompt: Explain the first three of the seven words from the cross (Luke 23; John 19).
sa.model: From the cross Jesus first prayed for His executioners, “Father, forgive them, for they do not know what they do.” To the penitent thief who asked to be remembered, He promised, “Today you will be with Me in Paradise,” that very day in conscious joy. And to His mother and the disciple John, He said, “Woman, behold your son... behold your mother,” caring for Mary even while dying.

sa.prompt: Explain the cry of dereliction and its meaning (Matt 27:46; Psalm 22).
sa.model: From the noon darkness Jesus cried, “My God, My God, why have You forsaken Me?” quoting Psalm 22. In that hour He bore the judgment our sin deserved, tasting in our place the forsaking that was ours, so that we might never be forsaken. It was not that the Father ceased to love the Son, but that the Son, bearing our sin, endured the abandonment sin deserves.

sa.prompt: Explain “It is finished” and the final word (John 19:30; Luke 23:46).
sa.model: Jesus cried, “It is finished,” one word in Greek, tetelestai, meaning the work of redemption was accomplished and the debt of sin paid in full. Then in willing surrender He said, “Father, into Your hands I commit My spirit,” and gave up His spirit. No man took His life; He laid it down. Even in dying He was Lord of His own death.

sa.prompt: Describe the signs at Jesus' death: the veil, the centurion, and the pierced side (Matt 27; John 19).
sa.model: At His death the temple veil was torn in two from top to bottom, opening the way into God's presence, for behind it stood the Most Holy Place where only the high priest could enter. The earth quaked, and the Roman centurion confessed, “Truly this was the Son of God.” A soldier pierced His side, and blood and water came out, proving He was truly dead, yet not a bone was broken, fulfilling the Passover lamb.

sa.prompt: Describe the burial of Jesus (John 19; Matt 27; Isaiah 53).
sa.model: Joseph of Arimathea, a secret disciple, took courage and asked Pilate for the body. With Nicodemus, who brought a hundred pounds of spices, he wrapped it in linen and laid it in his own new tomb cut from rock, rolling a great stone across the door. So He was with the rich in His death, as Isaiah foretold. The chief priests set a guard and sealed the stone.

sa.prompt: What does the cross mean, and how does Barabbas picture substitution?
sa.model: The cross means the Lamb of God was slain in our place. “It is finished” declares the price of sin paid in full; the torn veil declares the way to God opened; the forsaken cry shows He bore the judgment we deserved. Like Barabbas, the guilty go free because the innocent died. This is the gospel: the just died for the unjust to bring us to God, His death counted as ours.

sa.prompt: How do the divine and human stand together at the cross and tomb?
sa.model: The divine and human stand together: the eternal Son died as a man, commending His spirit to the Father, and the Lord of glory was wrapped in linen and laid in a borrowed grave. The death was real, the price was paid, the Lamb was slain. The stone was rolled, the seal set, the guard posted — yet in three days all of it would be undone, for the grave could not keep the Lamb of God.
